theorems.name: Contract Pathwise PV is Additive Over both
theorems.description: pathPV is additive over Contract.both: the pathwise present value of two combined contracts along one fixed scenario is the sum of their pathwise present values, for any discount curve D. Purely a finite-list-sum fact about pathPV -- no integral, measure or integrability hypothesis is involved yet.

import MathFin.Contracts.Core

open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {ι : Type*}

/-- `pathPV` is additive over `Contract.both`. -/
theorem pathPV_both' (D : ℝ≥0 → ℝ) (s : Scenario ι) (a b : Contract ι) :
    (Contract.both a b).pathPV D s = a.pathPV D s + b.pathPV D s :=
  MathFin.Contracts.Contract.pathPV_both D s a b

theorems.name: Contract Value is Additive Over both
theorems.description: Contract.value is additive over Contract.both, given both summands' discounted pathwise present values are Q-integrable: the value of a combined contract is the sum of the two values. Unlike value_scale (unconditional, since integral_const_mul holds even off the integrable set), this direction genuinely needs both integrability hypotheses -- integral_add is false without them.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Pricing

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {ι Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- `Contract.value` is additive over `both`, given both summands' discounted
pathwise present values are integrable. -/
theorem value_both' (Q : Measure Ω) (D : ℝ≥0 → ℝ)
    (X : ι → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ) (a b : Contract ι)
    (ha : Integrable (fun ω ↦ a.pathPV D (scenarioAt X ω)) Q)
    (hb : Integrable (fun ω ↦ b.pathPV D (scenarioAt X ω)) Q) :
    (Contract.both a b).value Q D X = a.value Q D X + b.value Q D X :=
  MathFin.Contracts.Contract.value_both Q D X a b ha hb

theorems.name: Value of Delivering a Martingale Asset
theorems.description: A contract that simply delivers a Q-martingale asset S at time T, undiscounted, is worth today's Q-expectation of S at time 0: value = integral S_0 dQ. Proved from Martingale.condExp_ae_eq chained through integral_condExp; needs only that S is a Q-martingale and Q a probability measure, no equivalent-martingale-measure (IsEMM) content.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Pricing

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- A contract that simply delivers a `Q`-martingale asset `S` at `T`,
undiscounted, is worth today's `Q`-expectation of `S` at time `0`. -/
theorem value_deliverAsset' {𝓕 : Filtration ℝ≥0 mΩ}
    {S : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    (hM : Martingale S 𝓕 Q) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    (Contract.pay T (Payoff.obs () T)).value Q (fun _ ↦ 1) (fun _ ↦ S)
      = ∫ ω, S 0 ω ∂Q :=
  MathFin.Contracts.Contract.value_deliverAsset hM T

theorems.name: Reified European Call Prices to the Black-Scholes Formula
theorems.description: The reified European call contract europeanCall K T -- a Payoff literally built from max, sub, obs and const nodes rather than an inline lambda -- prices under the single-asset Black-Scholes model to the closed-form call formula S_0 Phi(d_1) - K e^{-rT} Phi(d_2). The proof reduces Contract.value to the exact integral MathFin.bs_call_formula already computes; no new Black-Scholes content is proved here.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Models.BlackScholes

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- The reified European call prices to the Black-Scholes call formula. -/
theorem value_europeanCall' {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {S_0 K r σ : ℝ} {T : ℝ≥0} {Z : Ω → ℝ} (h : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K r σ T Z) :
    (europeanCall K T).value Q (fun _ ↦ Real.exp (-r * T)) (BlackScholes.assets S_0 r σ T Z)
      = S_0 * Phi (bsd1 S_0 K r σ T) - K * Real.exp (-r * T) * Phi (bsd2 S_0 K r σ T) :=
  MathFin.Contracts.BlackScholes.value_europeanCall h

theorems.name: Capped Call as a Composed Contract

theorems.name: Capped Call Value by Composition
theorems.description: The capped call's Black-Scholes value -- the price of cappedCall K1 K2 T under the single-asset Black-Scholes model -- is the difference of the two europeanCall closed forms, obtained by Contract.value_both and Contract.value_scale applied to value_europeanCall twice: composition, not a third integral, produces the price. The integrability hypotheses Contract.value_both would otherwise need are discharged internally (domination against the terminal asset price's Gaussian MGF), not left for the caller to supply.

import MathFin.Contracts.Models.BlackScholes

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- The capped call's Black-Scholes value is the difference of the two European
call values, by composition -- no integral is touched a third time. -/
theorem value_cappedCall' {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {S_0 K₁ K₂ r σ : ℝ} {T : ℝ≥0} {Z : Ω → ℝ}
    (h₁ : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K₁ r σ T Z) (h₂ : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K₂ r σ T Z) :
    (cappedCall K₁ K₂ T).value Q (fun _ ↦ Real.exp (-r * T)) (BlackScholes.assets S_0 r σ T Z)
      = (S_0 * Phi (bsd1 S_0 K₁ r σ T) - K₁ * Real.exp (-r * T) * Phi (bsd2 S_0 K₁ r σ T))
      - (S_0 * Phi (bsd1 S_0 K₂ r σ T) - K₂ * Real.exp (-r * T) * Phi (bsd2 S_0 K₂ r σ T)) :=
  MathFin.Contracts.BlackScholes.value_cappedCall h₁ h₂

theorems.name: Every Contract Is Integrable in a Bounded Model
theorems.description: In a model whose every coordinate X i t is measurable and bounded, every Contract's discounted pathwise payoff is integrable against any finite measure, so the additivity of Contract.value applies to any two contracts with no per-instrument integrability argument. Lognormal models such as Black-Scholes are not bounded and are not covered.

import MathFin.Contracts.Adapted

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin.Contracts

variable {ι Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- In a measurable, bounded model every contract's discounted payoff is integrable. -/
theorem integrable_pathPV_of_bounded' {Q : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure Q]
    (D : ℝ≥0 → ℝ) {X : ι → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hXm : ∀ i t, Measurable (X i t))
    (hXb : ∀ i t, ∃ C, ∀ ω, |X i t ω| ≤ C) (c : Contract ι) :
    Integrable (fun ω ↦ c.pathPV D (fun i t ↦ X i t ω)) Q :=
  Contract.integrable_pathPV_of_bounded D hXm hXb c

theorems.name: A European Payoff's Binomial Value Is Its Tree Price
theorems.description: In the binomial model with step length h and per-step rate rho (paths of i.i.d. coin flips that go up with probability q = crrUpProb u d rho, the underlying at time t the spot after floor(t/h) flips, cash discounted by e^(-rho t/h)), a single cash flow at a maturity T with T/h = N, paying g of the underlying at T, is worth the N-step backward-induction price binomialPrice u d rho g N S0. Only q in [0, 1] is assumed, not no-arbitrage.

import MathFin.Contracts.Models.Binomial

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

/-- A European payoff's value in the binomial model is its tree price. -/
theorem value_pay_eq_binomialPrice' {u d ρ h : ℝ} {q : ℝ≥0} (hq : q ≤ 1)
    (hqcrr : crrUpProb u d ρ = q) (S₀ : ℝ) {T : ℝ≥0} {N : ℕ} (hTN : (T : ℝ) / h = N)
    {a : Payoff Unit} {g : ℝ → ℝ} (hg : ∀ s : Scenario Unit, a.eval s = g (s () T)) :
    (Contract.pay T a).value (coinFlipMeasure q hq) (Binomial.discount ρ h)
        (Binomial.assets S₀ u d h)
      = binomialPrice u d ρ g N S₀ :=
  Binomial.value_pay_eq_binomialPrice hq hqcrr S₀ hTN hg

    (hqcrr : crrUpProb u d ρ = q) (S₀ K₁ K₂ : ℝ) {T : ℝ≥0} {N : ℕ}

theorems.name: A European Contract's Binomial Value Is the Cost of Its Hedge
theorems.description: In the binomial model under no-arbitrage, with paths drawn under the risk-neutral up-probability and S0 != 0, a single cash flow at T = N steps paying g of the underlying at T has a predictable strategy H in the discounted spot such that, on every path, the contract's discounted payoff equals its Contract.value plus the strategy's gains sum_{k<N} H_k (S~_{k+1} - S~_k).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Models.Binomial

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

/-- A European contract's binomial value is the cost of its hedge. -/
theorem pathPV_eq_value_add_gains' {u d ρ h : ℝ} {q : ℝ≥0} (hq : q ≤ 1)
    (hqcrr : crrUpProb u d ρ = q) (S₀ : ℝ) {T : ℝ≥0} {N : ℕ} (hTN : (T : ℝ) / h = N)
    (hna : BinomialNoArb u d ρ) (hS₀ : S₀ ≠ 0) {a : Payoff Unit} {g : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hg : ∀ s : Scenario Unit, a.eval s = g (s () T)) :
    ∃ H : ℕ → (ℕ → Bool) → ℝ, (∀ n, PathAdaptedAt n (H n)) ∧ ∀ ω,
      (Contract.pay T a).pathPV (Binomial.discount ρ h) (scenarioAt (Binomial.assets S₀ u d h) ω)
        = (Contract.pay T a).value (coinFlipMeasure q hq) (Binomial.discount ρ h)
            (Binomial.assets S₀ u d h)
          + ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N,
            H k ω * (discountedSpot S₀ u d ρ (k + 1) ω - discountedSpot S₀ u d ρ k ω) :=
  Binomial.pathPV_eq_value_add_gains hq hqcrr S₀ hTN hna hS₀ hg

theorems.name: One Contract in Two Models: CRR Value Converges to Black-Scholes Value
theorems.description: The European call europeanCall K T, a single contract term, priced in the n-step Cox-Ross-Rubinstein tree over [0, T] (step T/n, per-step rate rT/n, up and down factors e^(+-sigma sqrt(T/n)), up-probability crrProb r sigma T n), has values that converge as n -> infinity to its value in the Black-Scholes model, under the Black-Scholes hypotheses (S0, K, sigma, T > 0, standard normal driver) and |r| sqrt(T) < sigma.

import MathFin.Contracts.Models.BinomialLimit

open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped NNReal Topology
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- The call's value in the n-step CRR tree tends to its Black-Scholes value. -/
theorem tendsto_binomial_value_europeanCall' {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {S₀ K r σ : ℝ} {T : ℝ≥0} {Z : Ω → ℝ} (hbs : BSCallHyp Q S₀ K r σ T Z)
    (hrT : |r| * Real.sqrt T < σ) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (europeanCall K T).value
        (coinFlipMeasure (crrProb r σ T n).toNNReal (Real.toNNReal_le_one.mpr
          (crrProb_mem_Icc (fun _ hn ↦ binomialNoArb_crr hbs.T_pos hrT hn) n).2))
        (Binomial.discount (crrPerStepRate r T n) (crrStep T n))
        (Binomial.assets S₀ (crrUp σ T n) (crrDown σ T n) (crrStep T n))) atTop
      (𝓝 ((europeanCall K T).value Q (fun _ ↦ Real.exp (-r * T))
        (BlackScholes.assets S₀ r σ T Z))) :=
  tendsto_binomial_value_europeanCall hbs hrT

metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. tendsto_binomial_value_europeanCall in MathFin/Contracts/Models/BinomialLimit.lean composes three proved results: Binomial.value_europeanCall (each tree value is the n-step tree price, using T / (T/n) = n), binomialPrice_call_tendsto_bs_closed (MathFin/Binomial/CRRCharFun.lean and CRRClosedForm.lean: the CRR call prices converge to the Black-Scholes closed form, by characteristic functions, Levy continuity and put-call parity), and BlackScholes.value_europeanCall (that closed form is the Black-Scholes value of the same contract). The condition |r| sqrt(T) < sigma makes every tree with n >= 1 arbitrage-free (binomialNoArb_crr) and, with the degenerate n = 0 tree, keeps every up-probability in [0, 1] (crrProb_mem_Icc). European call only; no rate of convergence. Axioms-clean.
